the identification and characterization of autoantibodies to the integrin heterodimer α6β4 in patients with oral pemphiigoid.
the identification of the epitopes of the autoantibodies to integrin α6, which is the major autoantigen of the oral pemphighoid.
the pathogenesis of a disease that has a significant impact on the quality of life of patients.

the sera from American and Italians with OP are identical in their binding characteristics.

sera from patients with oral pemphiogid from the USA (Boston) and Italy (Naples) are identical in their recognition and binding of the α6 subunit of integrin, which is the major component of the hemidesmosome.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the anti‐α6 antibodies in sera of patients with OP are directed to a single region of integrin α6 and that this region is capable of inducing separation of the BMZ in vitro.

the anti‐α6 antibodies in sera from patients with oral pemhigoid recognize a single 245 AA fragment in the integrin α 6 chain, that this region is sufficient to induce blister formation in organ culture and that the reactivity of sera from patients in Naples, Italy and Boston, MA, are identical.
we have found an epitope in the human integrins that is recognized by autoantibodies of patients with OP and that this epitope causes blistering in organ culture.
